key_fields.sql: select z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone, count(t.pulocationid) as cash_trips from ops.zones z left join lake.trips t on t.pulocationid = z.locationid and t.payment_type = 2 group by z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone order by z.locationid
facts: lake.trips.pulocationid: 495833 rows, 495833 non-NULL, 243 distinct → NOT unique (repeated values)
lake.trips.payment_type: 495833 rows, 495833 non-NULL, 5 distinct → NOT unique (repeated values)

value.bottleneck: The hash join (node 8) forces a CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) on the probe side for ~99K filtered trips rows, preventing predicate pushdown and adding per-row conversion cost; the join then feeds 99K rows into a hash aggregation that only produces 265 groups.

hypotheses.claim: The CAST in the join condition (CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID) disables join-key partition pruning and forces a type conversion on every probe row; removing the cast or aligning column types would allow a faster hash join.

The hash join builds on the larger filtered trips input (~99K rows) instead of the tiny zones table (265 rows); forcing a build on zones (e.g., via join order hint or rewriting as aggregated subquery) would shrink the hash table and reduce probe cost.

The HASH_GROUP_BY processes 99K rows to produce only 265 groups; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID + payment_type before the join would reduce the join input cardinality by ~400x and eliminate the post-join aggregation.
